en: The Jātaka:
The Collection of Ten,
Chapter on the Four Gates (Catudvāravagga)
9. The Mahādhammapāla Jātaka “What is your vow?
What indeed is your holy life?
Of what well-practiced deed is this the fruition?”
"Tell me this matter, O brahmin:
why is it that among you the young do not die?
"We practice the Dhamma; we do not speak falsehood."
We avoid evil deeds;
we avoid everything that is ignoble.
Therefore, among us, the young do not die.
We listen to the Dhamma of both the non-virtuous and the virtuous,
yet we do not take pleasure in the Dhamma of the non-virtuous;
having abandoned the non-virtuous, we do not forsake the virtuous.
Therefore, indeed, our children do not die.
Before giving, we are joyful;
even while giving, we are truly glad at heart.
"Indeed, even after giving, we do not regret it later;
therefore, our children do not die young.
We [give] to ascetics, brahmins, and travelers."
To those who wander for alms, beggars, and the destitute,
we offer satisfaction with food and drink;
therefore, indeed, our children do not die.
We do not transgress against our wives,
nor do our wives transgress against us;
apart from them, we lead the holy life.
Therefore, indeed, we who are young do not die;
we all abstain from taking life and avoid what is not given in the world.
We do not drink intoxicants, nor do we speak falsehoods;
therefore, our children do not die young.
Indeed, they are born from these women who are well-behaved.
They are intelligent and possessed of abundant wisdom;
they are learned and masters of the Vedas.
Therefore, indeed, our youths do not die.
Mother and father, sisters and brothers,
sons and wives, and we ourselves— all of us— practice the Dhamma for the sake of the world beyond.
Therefore, indeed, our young ones do not die—
neither the male slaves, nor the female slaves, nor those who depend on us,
nor the attendants, nor all the laborers.
“They practice the Dhamma for the sake of the next world;
therefore, our children do not die.
Indeed, the Dhamma protects the one who lives according to the Dhamma.
The Dhamma well-practiced brings happiness;
this is the benefit when the Dhamma is well-practiced:
one who lives according to the Dhamma does not go to a state of woe.
Dhamma indeed protects the one who lives according to Dhamma,
like a great umbrella during the rainy season;
protected by Dhamma, I am a guardian of Dhamma.
"The bones of another; Prince Sukhī.
Thus ends the ninth Jātaka, the Mahādhammapāla Jātaka.
